topic: sub:11|Probability and data|Sets and set notation

parts.latex:
In a group of 60 students, 38 play basketball, 35 play hockey and 5 do not play either basketball or hockey.

How many students play both basketball and hockey?

solutions.latex:
Students who play at least one sport: $60-5=55$.

Using $n(B\cup H)=n(B)+n(H)-n(B\cap H)$:
$$\begin{aligned} 55 &= 38+35-n(B\cap H)\\ n(B\cap H) &= 73-55\\ &= 18\end{aligned}$$

2309.stem: A survey of 150 people found that 113 people liked swimming, 55 liked surfing and 15 liked neither.

figures.cap: Venn diagram of swim and surf with blank boxes
solution sketch: Venn diagram completed: swim only 80, both 33, surf only 22, neither 15

parts.latex:
Use this information to fill in the blank spaces in the Venn diagram.

\exfigure{292_q14_1}
If 2 people are selected at random, find the probability that both people like swimming only.

solutions.latex:
Total $150$, neither $15$, so $150-15=135$ like swimming or surfing or both.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{both}&=113+55-135=33\\\text{swimming only}&=113-33=80\\\text{surfing only}&=55-33=22\end{aligned}$$

\exfigure{292_q14_s1}

Swimming only $80$, both $33$, surfing only $22$, neither $15$.
criteria: Fills in two or three of the four regions correctly, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric was half a mark per box; rewritten top-down. Working for the region values added (source gave only the values). Checked: 80+33+22+15=150.

solutions.latex:
Both people are chosen from the $80$ who like swimming only, without replacement.
$$\begin{aligned}P&=\dfrac{80}{150}\times\dfrac{79}{149}\\&=\dfrac{632}{2235}\end{aligned}$$

parts.latex: In a group of 60 students, 24 have subscribed to SFLIX and 38 have subscribed to NETAN. If 12 students have subscribed to both SFLIX and NETAN, what is the probability that a student chosen at random has subscribed to neither SFLIX nor NETAN?

solutions.latex:
Students in SFLIX only: $24-12=12$.

Students in NETAN only: $38-12=26$.

Students in at least one: $12+12+26=50$, so $60-50=10$ are in neither.
$$P(\text{neither})=\dfrac{10}{60}=\dfrac{1}{6}$$
This is option B.
